about.title: Tehachapi Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Tehachapi residents rely on a small pool of local clinics and often travel toward Bakersfield for specialized or hospital-level care, which means questions about who's responsible for a bad outcome can get complicated fast. Maybe a diagnosis was delayed, a medication mix-up happened, or a surgical complication went unaddressed. Whatever brought you here, sorting out whether it's ordinary risk versus malpractice under California law takes a careful look at your records. Our team reviews what happened, explains your options under California's MICRA rules, and tells you honestly whether you have a case worth pursuing. There's no obligation and no cost to find out. A bad outcome by itself isn't proof of a mistake, but you deserve a real answer, not a guess.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Wait

items.title: The Clock Moves Faster Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim — so early review matters.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a lawsuit can even be filed, California law requires a 90-day notice to the healthcare provider, which affects how soon your case needs to get moving.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A qualified medical expert typically has to weigh in to support a malpractice claim, and our team can help arrange that kind of evaluation.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that not every complication or disappointing result means a provider was negligent. We need to review whether the care fell below the accepted medical standard, which is why a proper case evaluation matters before assuming anything.

items.question: I live in Tehachapi but was treated in Bakersfield — does that matter?
items.answer: It can affect where a claim is filed and which providers are involved, but it doesn't stop you from getting help. Our team is familiar with Kern County cases and can sort out those details for you.

items.question: What does California's damages cap mean for my case?
items.answer: MICRA places a cap on non-economic damages — things like pain and suffering — and that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, like medical bills and lost income, aren't limited the same way, and we can walk you through how that applies to your situation.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. We offer free case reviews, and we generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
